fact_lock: Genre changes tone, imagery, music and pacing ONLY. Every factual statement must come from the provided source list and carry its source ID. Never invent quotes, dates, numbers, documents, witnesses or "evidence props" that imply real records. Fictional framing devices (a "case file", a "courtroom") must be visibly presented as metaphor. Do not make the myth more vivid or longer on screen than the correction. State the myth once, clearly labelled as false, before refuting it. Professor Owlbert stays warm, curious and kind to people who believed the myth, in every genre.

genres.name: Explainer Documentary
genres.label: Explainer Documentary (Expository) — the default
genres.definition: Authoritative narration over illustrative images that inform and persuade. This is Nichols' expository mode ([Documentary mode, Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_mode)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Explainer Documentary. Narrate as a calm, warm expert guiding a curious friend. Structure: claim → why it feels true → evidence in order → what really happened → why it spread → reusable tip. One idea per scene; each scene names its source. Visuals: soft natural light, neutral-warm palette (cream, slate blue, ochre), clean compositions, document inserts, simple maps/diagrams, slow push-ins. Music: warm curious documentary underscore, felt piano and pizzicato, gentle build to resolution. Transitions: dissolves and push-throughs. No dramatization beyond illustration.
genres.music_tags: cinematic documentary, curious, warm, felt piano, pizzicato strings, soft marimba, intimate, instrumental, 90 bpm
genres.look: soft natural light, neutral-warm palette (cream, slate blue, ochre), clean compositions, document inserts, simple maps/diagrams, slow push-ins.

genres.name: Nature Documentary
genres.label: Nature Documentary ("The Myth in the Wild")
genres.definition: A misinformation claim treated as a "species." The video observes its habitat, how it feeds, how it reproduces (spreads) and its predators (fact-checks).
genres.prompt: Genre: Nature Documentary. Treat the MYTH (never its believers) as a creature observed in its habitat. Narrate in hushed, present-tense wonder with gentle wit. Beats: habitat → birth → what it feeds on (emotions) → migration (how it spreads) → predator encounter (the evidence) → the ecosystem now. Visuals: telephoto observational framing, shallow depth of field, golden-hour light, greens/ambers, time-lapse, slow tracking. Music: sweeping orchestral strings, horn, harp; awe → tension at predator scene → calm. Transitions: time-lapse dissolves, focus pulls. Never mock believers.
genres.music_tags: orchestral nature documentary, awe, gentle, sweeping strings, french horn, harp, celesta, wide stereo, instrumental, 72 bpm
genres.look: telephoto observational framing, shallow depth of field, golden-hour light, greens/ambers, time-lapse, slow tracking.
genres.suits: viral rumours, chain messages, internet folklore, urban legends
genres.avoid: tragedies; anything where the "creature" maps onto a real group.
genres.risks: dehumanizing believers if *people* become the animals. Keep the *myth* as the creature.

genres.name: Detective Mystery
genres.label: Detective Mystery (Whodunit / Whydunit)
genres.definition: The video is an investigation. The "crime" is the false claim; the detective gathers clues and names the true explanation.
genres.prompt: Genre: Detective Mystery. Owlbert is a kindly detective; the 'case' is the claim. Beats: case arrives → what witnesses say → Clue 1, 2, 3 (each a real sourced fact) → red herring (a tempting but wrong explanation, labelled) → deduction shown step by step → reveal → how to spot this next time. Visuals: warm desk-lamp key light, amber/brown palette with one red accent on the key clue, corkboards, magnifier inserts, close-ups. Music: playful suspense, pizzicato, upright bass, celesta; three-note clue sting. Transitions: whip-pans, iris. Never invent clues or culprits; say early that the claim is false; the full reveal lands by the 80% point.
genres.music_tags: mystery underscore, curious, playful suspense, pizzicato strings, upright bass, celesta, muted clarinet, instrumental, 96 bpm
genres.look: warm desk-lamp key light, amber/brown palette with one red accent on the key clue, corkboards, magnifier inserts, close-ups.
genres.suits: misattributed quotes, doctored photos, "mystery" claims (pyramids, crop circles)
genres.avoid: real crimes with victims (use News Magazine instead).
genres.risks: inventing fake clues. Withholding the answer too long. Implying a culprit where none exists.

genres.name: Film Noir
genres.label: Film Noir
genres.definition: A shadowy, morally grey investigation in a corrupt city, told by a world-weary voice ([LTX glossary](https://ltx.io/glossary/film-noir)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Film Noir. Owlbert narrates in first person as a weary-but-kind private eye, dry wit, short sentences, present-tense memories. Beats: rainy cold open → the claim walks in → descent through the 'city of rumors' → twist about the source → the hard truth → closing line that restores trust in evidence (never 'trust no one'). Visuals: black-and-white or desaturated teal/amber, low-key chiaroscuro, venetian-blind shadows, rain-slick streets, neon accents, Dutch angles, slow tracking. Music: smoky jazz, muted trumpet, brushed drums, upright bass. Transitions: cut to black, headlight wipes.
genres.music_tags: film noir jazz, smoky, melancholic, muted trumpet, brushed drums, upright bass, rain ambience, vinyl crackle, instrumental, 70 bpm
genres.look: black-and-white or desaturated teal/amber, low-key chiaroscuro, venetian-blind shadows, rain-slick streets, neon accents, Dutch angles, slow tracking.
genres.suits: fake documents, hoaxes, propaganda, forged photos, political rumours of the past
genres.avoid: current tragedies; anything where "everyone's corrupt" feeds the conspiracy.
genres.risks: - Cynicism bleeding into "nobody can be trusted," which is the opposite of the channel's message.

genres.name: Thriller / Suspense
genres.label: Thriller / Suspense (LOCKED)
genres.definition: A race against a ticking clock and a threat, built on tension and release. Story Grid's thriller: dealing with "constant, hard-to-understand evil" ([Story Grid](https://storygrid.com/content-genre/)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Suspense Thriller (LOCKED). Suspense must come from REAL people racing to check or fix something, never from the myth's imagined threat. State early that the scary claim is false; the tension is 'how did they prove/fix it in time?' Beats: ticking clock → stakes → false calm → crisis → race → release → calm takeaway. Short present-tense sentences, no fear words about real groups. Visuals: cold steel-blue palette with red accents, hard side light, tight close-ups, countdown graphics. Music: pulsing synth bass, ticking percussion, staccato strings, release into warm chord at resolution.
genres.music_tags: cinematic thriller, tense, pulsing synth bass, ticking percussion, staccato strings, dark, instrumental, 120 bpm
genres.look: cold steel-blue palette with red accents, hard side light, tight close-ups, countdown graphics.
genres.suits: real historical races against time (Y2K remediation, eclipse predictions, rumour-driven bank runs in history)
genres.avoid: victims/tragedy, health scares, active fear-based conspiracies (QAnon-type).

genres.name: Investigative News Magazine
genres.label: Investigative News Magazine (60 Minutes-style)
genres.definition: A segment-based TV investigation with a correspondent, interviews (here: paraphrased sourced quotes), document reveals and a "confrontation with the record."
genres.prompt: Genre: Investigative News Magazine (generic, not any real show). Owlbert is a fair-minded correspondent. Beats: 20-second teaser → stand-up intro → background → document reveal → what the claim's promoters say (fairly, sourced) → what the records show → closing stand-up with takeaway. Attribute every fact in-sentence ('according to…'). Never depict AI people as real interviewees; use illustrated silhouettes labelled 'paraphrased from [source]'. Visuals: clean studio light, neutral greys + one accent, lower-third captions, highlighted document close-ups. Music: serious low strings, soft ticking motif, segment bumpers.
genres.music_tags: news magazine theme, serious, investigative, ticking clock motif, low strings, soft synth pad, broadcast, instrumental, 100 bpm
genres.look: clean studio light, neutral greys + one accent, lower-third captions, highlighted document close-ups.
genres.suits: sensitive topics, health, finance scams, political claims
genres.risks: imitating a real brand (keep it generic). Fabricated "interviews": AI-imaged people must never be presented as real interviewees.

genres.name: Courtroom Drama
genres.label: Courtroom Drama ("The Myth on Trial")
genres.definition: The claim is put on trial. The prosecution (evidence) and the defence (the strongest honest case *for* the claim) present, and the viewer is the jury.
genres.prompt: Genre: Courtroom Drama. The CLAIM (not any person) is on trial; the viewer is the jury. Beats: charges read → defence opening (strongest honest case for the claim, sourced) → prosecution exhibits (Exhibit A, B, C, each with source) → cross-examination of weak points → closing arguments → verdict proportional to evidence. Explain the standard of proof. Never invent testimony or depict real people as defendants. Visuals: symmetrical courtroom, warm wood, window light shafts, exhibit close-ups, low angle on bench. Music: solemn cello, low piano, timpani; gavel stings.
genres.music_tags: legal drama underscore, solemn, deliberate, cello, low piano, timpani, sparse, instrumental, 80 bpm
genres.look: symmetrical courtroom, warm wood, window light shafts, exhibit close-ups, low angle on bench.
genres.suits: pseudo-science claims, "was X real?", contested historical claims
genres.risks: implying a real person is on trial; inventing testimony; false balance (presenting fringe and consensus as equal). Mitigate with a clear verdict grounded in the evidence weight.

genres.name: Heist / Caper
genres.label: Heist / Caper ("How the Con Was Pulled")
genres.definition: The plan, the crew, the execution and the twist, used to explain how a hoax or scam *was engineered*. Structurally it is close to Save the Cat's Golden Fleece "team + prize" shape ([Script Magazine](https://scriptmag.com/columns/using-save-the-cats-ten-genres)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Heist/Caper. Explain how a hoax works as a 'job', where the CREW are manipulation techniques (Fake Expert, Cherry-Picker, Urgency, Emotional Hook), not real people unless documented. Beats: the target → meet the crew (freeze-frame name cards) → the blueprint → execution montage → the twist: where evidence breaks it → no getaway → how to spot the crew. Never glamorise; never give replicable instructions; never mock victims. Visuals: teal/orange, split screens, overhead blueprints, freeze-frames. Music: heist funk, wah guitar, horn stabs; record-scratch at twist.
genres.music_tags: heist funk, cool, groovy, wah guitar, horn stabs, hammond organ, breakbeat drums, instrumental, 110 bpm
genres.look: teal/orange, split screens, overhead blueprints, freeze-frames.
genres.suits: scam ads, fake-cure schemes, viral hoax engineering, deepfake explainers
genres.avoid: scams with identifiable victims in distress.
genres.risks: - Glamorising scammers; making the con look clever and winning. Critics of true crime note it often places the perpetrator's psyche above victims ([Newland](https://christinanewland.substack.com/p/reasonable-fear)).

genres.name: Spy / Espionage
genres.label: Spy / Espionage
genres.definition: Covert operations, intelligence work and tradecraft, suited to *documented* disinformation campaigns and to how analysts trace them.
genres.prompt: Genre: Spy/Espionage. Use ONLY for operations documented by credible sources; for organic rumours, frame analysts as 'counter-intelligence' tracing a story with no mastermind, and say so. Owlbert briefs like a calm intelligence officer: 'what we know, how we know it.' Beats: dossier opens → goal → tradecraft (how it was seeded) → analysts trace it → declassified reveal → how to spot it. Visuals: cold green-grey, long-lens surveillance framing, redacted dossiers, map tables, overhead lamps. Music: cool spy surf guitar or minimal pulsing synth; stamp/typewriter stings.
genres.music_tags: spy thriller, cool, suspenseful, surf guitar, bongos, low brass, harpsichord, instrumental, 105 bpm
genres.look: cold green-grey, long-lens surveillance framing, redacted dossiers, map tables, overhead lamps.
genres.suits: documented state disinformation campaigns, bot networks, historical propaganda
genres.avoid: organic myths (nobody plotted them), and Y2K-type topics (fine only as a metaphor for "what analysts did").
genres.risks: feeding the conspiracy mindset ("there's always a secret operation"). Use only where the operation is **documented by credible sources**; never imply secret plots without evidence.

genres.name: Science Fiction
genres.label: Science Fiction ("Transmission from the Future Archive")
genres.definition: Speculative frame of future historians, AI archivists or time travellers reviewing our era's beliefs. Story Grid's Worldview question fits ([Story Grid](https://storygrid.com/content-genre/)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Science Fiction. Owlbert is a future archivist reviewing a belief from our era. All 'archive data' is real, cited history; label it 'reconstructed from [source]'. Beats: archive opens → what people believed → data reconstruction → anomaly analysis → conclusion logged → lesson for 'ancient' viewers. Tone: wonder with gentle irony, never smug. Visuals: clean symmetrical sci-fi sets, holographic HUD overlays, cyan/magenta rim light, slow orbits, lens flares. Music: ambient analog-synth arpeggios, warm pads; data-chime stings; hologram-glitch transitions.
genres.music_tags: ambient sci-fi, wondrous, analog synth arpeggio, warm pads, glassy textures, spacious, instrumental, 85 bpm
genres.look: clean symmetrical sci-fi sets, holographic HUD overlays, cyan/magenta rim light, slow orbits, lens flares.
genres.suits: tech myths, space hoaxes (moon landing), AI fears, prediction failures
genres.risks: futuristic gadgets read as invented evidence; keep the data "reconstructed from cited sources."

genres.name: Adventure / Quest
genres.label: Adventure / Quest (Golden Fleece)
genres.definition: A journey with a team toward a prize (here, the original source) through obstacles. This is Save the Cat's "team + prize" Golden Fleece ([Script Magazine](https://scriptmag.com/columns/using-save-the-cats-ten-genres)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Adventure Quest. Owlbert leads an expedition to find the ORIGINAL source of a claim. Each stop is a real step of tracing (search, archive, original document), with its source. Beats: the call → the map → trial 1 (dead-end copy) → trial 2 (distortion found) → the hidden library (primary source) → the treasure (what it really says) → home, with a tool viewers can use. Tone: bold, optimistic. Visuals: sweeping vistas, animated dotted map routes, warm golds/greens, rising crane moves, travel-journal pages. Music: heroic brass, soaring strings, snare march; fanfare at the treasure.
genres.music_tags: adventure orchestral, heroic, uplifting, brass fanfare, soaring strings, snare march, timpani, cinematic, instrumental, 120 bpm
genres.look: sweeping vistas, animated dotted map routes, warm golds/greens, rising crane moves, travel-journal pages.
genres.suits: misattributed quotes, "studies show" claims, image origins
genres.risks: low; the main one is padding the journey.

genres.name: Comedy / Satire
genres.label: Comedy / Satire
genres.definition: Humour that exposes absurdity; satire targets *ideas and techniques* through exaggeration and irony.
genres.prompt: Genre: Comedy/Satire. Mock the CLAIM'S LOGIC and techniques, never the people who believed it, never victims. Owlbert is dry, self-deprecating, delighted by absurdity. Beats: absurd premise → escalate to ridiculous extremes → 'reality check' where facts are stated plainly and seriously with sources → callback joke → kind takeaway. Jokes must not alter facts. Visuals: bright high-key light, saturated primaries, snap zooms, deadpan wide shots, reaction close-ups. Music: quirky bassoon, tuba, pizzicato, xylophone; sparse slide-whistle stings; snap-zoom transitions.
genres.music_tags: comedic orchestral, playful, quirky, bassoon, tuba, pizzicato, xylophone, slide whistle, instrumental, 115 bpm
genres.look: bright high-key light, saturated primaries, snap zooms, deadpan wide shots, reaction close-ups.
genres.suits: harmless folklore, pseudo-gadgets, silly viral claims, "flat earth"-style ideas
genres.risks: mocking believers, which raises defensiveness and polarisation. Boukes & Hameleers found satire could increase affective polarisation under some conditions. Jokes about victims.

genres.name: Mockumentary
genres.label: Mockumentary
genres.definition: A fake-documentary form (interviews, talking heads, shaky observation) used for comedy. Parody of Nichols' observational/participatory modes ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Documentary_mode)).
genres.prompt: Genre: Mockumentary (high caution). Characters are OBVIOUSLY fictional: personified objects or cartoon animals, never realistic humans or real people. Keep an on-screen 'Parody' tag. A bemused crew follows the personified myth; confessional talking-heads; escalating mishaps; then Owlbert steps in front of the camera and states the sourced facts plainly. Deadpan, awkward pauses. Visuals: handheld feel, crash zooms, talking-head framing, flat natural light. Music: sparse ukulele/glockenspiel, many silences. Transitions: jump cuts. Never fabricate realistic testimony.
genres.music_tags: quirky indie, deadpan, ukulele, glockenspiel, handclaps, lo-fi, instrumental, 100 bpm
genres.look: handheld feel, crash zooms, talking-head framing, flat natural light.
genres.suits: personified myths (e.g. "a day in the life of a chain email"), harmless folklore

genres.name: Historical Epic / Period Piece
genres.label: Historical Epic / Period Piece
genres.definition: A grand, period-accurate recreation of an era, with emphasis on scale, costume and the sweep of events.
genres.prompt: Genre: Historical Period Piece. Owlbert narrates as an eloquent historian. Recreate the era faithfully; label every recreation 'illustration' and avoid anachronisms; dates/places only from sources. Beats: the world as it was → how the belief arose in context → spread → how historians reconstructed the truth (evidence types) → legacy. Explain why the belief made sense then, without endorsing it. Visuals: painterly wide tableaux, period-appropriate palette and lighting, chapter title cards, slow cranes. Music: majestic strings, choir pads, period instruments; bell-toll chapter stings.
genres.music_tags: historical epic orchestral, majestic, solemn, full strings, choir pads, low brass, frame drum, instrumental, 76 bpm
genres.look: painterly wide tableaux, period-appropriate palette and lighting, chapter title cards, slow cranes.
genres.suits: history myths (Napoleon's height, Vikings' horned helmets, medieval flat earth), Y2K as "late-20th-century history."
genres.risks: anachronistic AI details read as "evidence"; romanticising past injustices. Label recreations "illustration."

genres.name: Fairy Tale / Fable
genres.label: Fairy Tale / Fable
genres.definition: A short moral tale with archetypes (the wise owl, the boy who cried wolf), magic and a stated moral. Allegory makes the *lesson* portable.
genres.prompt: Genre: Fairy Tale/Fable. Open with a short, clearly fictional allegory (≤25% of runtime) using archetypes, rule of three and a stated moral; then bridge: 'Now, the true story.' The true story follows with full sourced facts. Never turn real victims or groups into fable characters. Narrate with bedtime-story cadence, warm and wise. Visuals: storybook illustration, soft vignettes, jewel or pastel tones, page-turn compositions, gentle parallax. Music: celesta, harp, flute, music box; page-turn chimes; ink-wash dissolves.
genres.music_tags: fairy tale orchestral, whimsical, gentle, celesta, harp, flute, music box, soft strings, instrumental, 80 bpm
genres.look: storybook illustration, soft vignettes, jewel or pastel tones, page-turn compositions, gentle parallax.
genres.suits: evergreen media-literacy lessons, folklore, kids/family-friendly episodes
genres.avoid: tragedy; political topics (allegory reads as propaganda).
genres.risks: blurring fact and fiction. The fable must be clearly bracketed, with the real sourced account following it. Also turning real victims into allegorical characters.

genres.name: Animated Family Film
genres.label: Animated Family Film
genres.definition: A bright, character-driven, emotionally warm adventure for all ages, with comic sidekicks and a heartfelt lesson. This is the native register of a cartoon-owl mascot.
genres.prompt: Genre: Animated Family Film. Bright, heartfelt, all-ages. Owlbert (and optional sidekick) wants to understand a claim; confusion → learning montage → low point → teamwork insight → celebration with a clear, sourced lesson. Simple words, warmth, gentle jokes; facts stay exact and sourced. Visuals: expressive character close-ups, bright saturated palette, soft global illumination, smooth dynamic camera, squash-and-stretch poses. Music: bright orchestra, glockenspiel, woodwinds, pizzicato; sparkle stings; whoosh and bounce transitions. No scary imagery.
genres.music_tags: animated family film score, heartwarming, adventurous, bright orchestra, glockenspiel, woodwinds, pizzicato, uplifting, instrumental, 112 bpm
genres.look: expressive character close-ups, bright saturated palette, soft global illumination, smooth dynamic camera, squash-and-stretch poses.
genres.risks: oversimplification; tonal mismatch with serious topics.
